Reality Layers — Absolute • Intersubjective • Subjective

Strict 'objective reality' is not available; what we rely on is robust intersubjective objectivity that is good enough to build bridges — and also humble enough to be revised.

The three layers of 'reality'

  • Absolute/Unknowable
  • Intersubjective (science, culture, shared models)
  • Subjective (personal perception/dream).

Think of experience as a stack. The Absolute may exist independently but is epistemically out of reach. The Intersubjective layer stabilizes common models via measurement, replication, and norms of inquiry. The Subjective layer is each person’s constructed stream (waking perception, memory, dreaming).

  • Subjective layer: Each mind constructs a world via predictive processing; memories are reconstructed; dreams reveal the engine running offline.
  • Intersubjective layer: We stabilize models by triangulating with others, instruments, and methods (replication, error-correction). This yields pragmatic objectivity.
  • Absolute layer: There may be a mind-independent reality (Kant’s noumenon), but we access it only through the layers below. It’s a regulative ideal, not a direct deliverable.
